module

public import Mathlib.Topology.Defs.Induced
public import Mathlib.Topology.Separation.Regular
public import Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousOn

@[expose] public section

universe u

/--
A topological space `X` is an *absolute neighborhood retract* (ANR) if, whenever it is
embedded as a closed subspace of a normal space `Y`, there exists a continuous retraction
from some open neighborhood of `X` in `Y` onto `X`.

More precisely, for every closed embedding `e : X → Y` into a normal space `Y`, there
exist an open set `U ⊆ Y` containing the image of `e` and a continuous map `r : Y → X`
defined on `U` such that `r ∘ e = id`.
-/
class IsAbsoluteNeighborhoodRetract (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_neighborhood_retract (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [NormalSpace Y] (e : X → Y) :
    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding e → ∃ (U : Set Y) (r : Y → X),
      IsOpen U ∧ Set.range e ⊆ U ∧ ContinuousOn r U ∧ ∀ x : X, r (e x) = x

findings.description: The class does not require X to belong to the chosen category of normal spaces. Consequently, every nonnormal space satisfies it vacuously: a closed embedding into a normal Y would imply NormalSpace X by Mathlib's Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.normalSpace. I proved this implication in Lean and constructed a concrete example on Fin 3 with opens ∅, {0}, {0,1}, {0,2}, and univ. This space is not normal (the closed sets {1} and {2} cannot be separated), but it satisfies IsAbsoluteNeighborhoodRetract. This is not the standard class-relative ANR notion, even accepting the docstring's choice of normal ambient spaces.
findings.source_evidence: Mardešić, “Absolute Neighborhood Retracts and Shape Theory,” §1, p. 242, defines an AR/ANR for a class C as a space belonging to C with the appropriate retraction property. https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/mardesic.pdf. The class-membership requirement is also explicit at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retraction_(topology)#Absolute_neighborhood_retract_(ANR). Mathlib.Topology.Separation.Regular proves that closed embeddings into normal spaces have normal domains.
findings.suggested_fix: Require membership in the selected category. If retaining normal ambient spaces, make the class extend NormalSpace X (or require that instance as a parameter). If adopting the standard metric ANR notion, require MetrizableSpace X and quantify over metrizable ambient spaces. A repair retaining the normal category is tested in /workspace/review/corrected_definition.lean.

findings.description: The witness r : Y → X must be a total function, although a neighborhood retraction should be defined only on U. This incorrectly excludes the empty space. Empty embeds as a closed subspace of PUnit, but no function PUnit → Empty exists, regardless of U. The ordinary neighborhood property holds for Empty by choosing U = ∅ and its unique map to Empty. Both assertions are proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. More precisely, I proved that the current class is equivalent to Nonempty X conjoined with the same normal-ambient retraction property using maps U → X. Thus totality is harmless for nonempty X, but introduces an unintended nonemptiness requirement globally.
findings.source_evidence: Halverson–Repovš, “The Bing-Borsuk and the Busemann Conjectures,” §2, defines the retraction as a continuous surjection r : U → e(X), fixing e(X), not as a function on the whole ambient space: https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886v2. The neighborhood-retract definitions in Mardešić §1 and https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Retract_of_a_topological_space likewise require a retraction only from an open neighborhood; this permits the empty neighborhood of the empty space.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a subtype-domain witness: ∃ (U : Set Y) (hU : Set.range e ⊆ U) (r : U → X), IsOpen U ∧ Continuous r ∧ ∀ x, r ⟨e x, hU ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩ = x. This admits the empty space without imposing a nonstandard nonemptiness convention.

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/BingBorsuk.lean, the ANR hypothesis uses the reviewed class's normal-ambient version, while both cited sources define ANR using metrizable ambient spaces. These categories are genuinely different, even for nonempty metrizable X: the Hanner–Dowker characterization additionally requires separability and complete metrizability for ANR(normal). For example, c₀₀ with its ℓ² norm is a metric AR but is not completely metrizable, hence is not ANR(normal). That example establishes a difference between the definitions, not a counterexample within this finite-dimensional conjecture. I did not establish whether the other hypotheses or the source's intended domain make the replacement equivalent, so this is a modelling concern rather than a definite misformalization of the conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: The definitions section of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing%E2%80%93Borsuk_conjecture and §2 of https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886v2 explicitly quantify over embeddings into metric spaces. McCandless, “On a theorem of Hanner and Dowker,” Portugaliae Mathematica 26 (1967), pp. 479–482, restates the characterization ANR(normal) = separable absolute-Gδ metric ANR and discusses its proof: https://purl.pt/2560. Mardešić, §1, pp. 242–243, specifies the metric convention and the metric-AR property of convex subsets of normed spaces.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide and use the metrizable-ambient ANR definition, with retractions defined on the neighborhood. State any intended separability/local-compactness restrictions explicitly. Alternatively, retain the normal-space variant but document and justify its equivalence to the cited formulation on the conjecture's intended domain.

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], with a module comment saying the conjecture remains open above dimensions 1 and 2.
status_issues.source_status: Later literature reports Bryant–Ferry counterexamples in every dimension n ≥ 6. Valov's 2023 survey explicitly leaves dimensions 3, 4, and 5 open. His published TAMS article, electronically published in October 2024 and appearing in 2025, repeats the counterexample announcement (first announced in 2018, revised announcement in 2023) and explicitly discusses their existence.
status_issues.evidence: Valov, Homogeneous locally compact spaces, Introduction: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00341v1. Corroborating published source: Valov, Local structure of homogeneous ANR-spaces, Introduction, DOI 10.1090/tran/9296, https://faculty.nipissingu.ca/veskov/files/2025/06/Local_StructureTAMS.pdf. It reports counterexamples “for every n ≥ 6” and then says “Despite the existence of counterexamples to the Bing-Borsuk conjecture”. These are compact metric ANRs, so the normal-ambient ANR restriction does not avoid the reported counterexamples.
status_issues.suggested_change: Update the all-dimensional conjecture's status to research solved with a negative formulation (negate the universal assertion, or use answer(False) ↔ that assertion), and retain separate open variants for dimensions 3–5. Cite the later literature and the Bryant–Ferry counterexample announcement/preprint.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion is only Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X), whereas Halverson–Repovš define an n-manifold as a separable metric, locally Euclidean space. Hausdorffness and countability are not explicit in the conclusion.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the hypotheses actually present, MetrizableSpace X implies Hausdorffness. The stronger normal-ambient ANR property, for metrizable X, implies separability by Hanner–Dowker; separable metrizable spaces are second countable. A ChartedSpace over Fin n → ℝ supplies local homeomorphisms to open subsets of ℝⁿ, equivalently the usual locally Euclidean condition. Thus these omitted conclusion requirements are not an additional defect. The Hausdorff equivalence and the countability equivalence assuming separability were checked in Lean; the Hanner–Dowker implication itself was checked only in the literature.

review.notes: The file contains one class and its projection, with no additional hand-written lemmas or instances. Searches found one problem use site and no existing Mathlib ANR definition; TietzeExtension is related but not a duplicate. All finalized Lean experiments compile in /workspace/review/: scratch.lean proves the empty-space failure, the exact Nonempty/subtype characterization, and nonnormal vacuity; finite.lean proves the three-point counterexample and computationally enumerates its opens; corrected_definition.lean tests repairs; use_site_boundary.lean and conclusion_check.lean check the consumer's boundary cases and implied separation/countability properties. The proved results have no sorryAx dependency. The empty-space defect does not itself give a bad Bing–Borsuk instance, since Empty satisfies its charted-space conclusion; metrizable X also rules out nonnormal vacuity. The status item follows the later published source, not an independent verification of the unavailable Bryant–Ferry preprint. The reviewed file and consumer were left unchanged.

The required compilation completed without errors or warnings; scratch regression tests verify the empty-space, singleton, and nonnormal-space cases.

module

public import Mathlib.Topology.Defs.Induced
public import Mathlib.Topology.Separation.Regular
public import Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousOn

@[expose] public section

universe u

/--
A normal topological space `X` is an *absolute neighborhood retract* (ANR) for normal spaces
if, whenever it is embedded as a closed subspace of a normal space `Y`, there exists a
continuous retraction from some open neighborhood of `X` in `Y` onto `X`.

More precisely, for every closed embedding `e : X → Y` into a normal space `Y`, there
exist an open set `U ⊆ Y` containing the image of `e` and a continuous map `r : U → X`
which is a left inverse to the induced embedding `X → U`.
-/
class IsAbsoluteNeighborhoodRetract (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop
    extends NormalSpace X where
  exists_neighborhood_retract (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [NormalSpace Y] (e : X → Y) :
    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding e → ∃ (U : Set Y) (hU : Set.range e ⊆ U) (r : U → X),
      IsOpen U ∧ Continuous r ∧ ∀ x : X, r ⟨e x, hU ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩ = x
